head: what the proposal changes
why
rows: adds: tokens of the richest agent, as a share of all tokens (at most 0.1)

no ruler: as the hub line asks that no agent hold too many of the links, this asks it of tokens; a world unequal everywhere is healthy, one agent holding the world's fortune is not (the author, 2026-11-08: at most 10%)
adds: same-position share: of two agents in the same situation, how often they act measurably differently (at least 0.5)
the author's own number for very different behaviours surviving (2026-10-24), with its line at half: two agents more often act differently than alike
adds: Gini of the tokens, over the Gini of tokens dealt out at random at the same mean holding (at least 1)

with no baseline, chance draws the line: a world more even than a random deal has something flattening it; tokens dealt out at random, one at least, at a mean of m an agent have a Gini of (m - 1) / (2m - 1), so the line moves with the world's own riches (0.40 at 3 tokens an agent, 0.46 at 7, 0.47 at 10)
adds: big culls: pieces of more than 15% of the network culled at once, every hundred iterations (at most 1)

the author's sixth criterion (2026-11-08): leaves culled everywhere are no harm, a whole branch culled every few iterations is; a piece is big past the author's bar for what one loss may cut off (15%), and a world may lose one about once every hundred iterations

a genotype is renewed by every mutation, so how many agents share one says how seldom brains mutate, not how differently agents act; the same-position share measures that (in round 3 no world came near the line: at most 26% of a world's agents shared a genotype)
drawn at B2's most even world of Experiment 16, a baseline the screen no longer compares with; the proposal's line for not too even is drawn by chance instead

order.title: The living worlds, most healthy first
order.caption: Each of the 82 worlds that lived to the end of its run is a row, ranked by its health, the sum of its criteria's scores; each criterion is a column, coloured by how much of what it asks the world has, from none (dark) to all of it (bright yellow): a criterion is met as far as its weakest line. A world named "w" or "s" is one of the eight draws played a token at a time, weakest first or strongest first. The 18 worlds that died are not shown: they come last in the order.
order.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From the screen's readings of every world, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/screen/worlds/<run>.json` (research/screen/measures.py: every iteration's statistics, every 25th iteration's frame, every kept world), scored by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.

1. Average every number of a world over iterations 100 to the end of its run (the judge's averages, `research/screen/measures.py`).
2. For each line, the share of what it asks that the world has, counted from the line's floor (`progress` in `health.py`), at most 1.
3. Each criterion: its weakest line's share. Health: the sum over the criteria.
4. Rank the living worlds by health, ties by their weakest criterion.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py healthorder`.

lines.title: Every line of the proposal, against the living worlds
lines.caption: One chart a measure: each dot is a living world's average of it, from iteration 100 to the end of its run, and each dashed line is a line drawn on it; the short bar is the median. The title says which side passes and how many of the living worlds meet every line on the chart. The dots are spread sideways only so that they do not hide each other.
lines.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From the screen's readings of every world, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/screen/worlds/<run>.json` (research/screen/measures.py: every iteration's statistics, every 25th iteration's frame, every kept world), scored by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.

1. Read each living world's averages from `health.json`.
2. One dot per world and measure; each line's value as a guide.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py healthorder`.

culls.title: Leaves or branches: what the worlds lose at once
culls.caption: Each dot is a living world. Across, how much of its network an average phase culls (cuts off from the largest piece and removes), every piece counted, from leaves culled one by one to whole branches; up, how often a single piece of more than 15% of the network was culled at once, every 100 iterations (iterations 100 to the end of the run). Agents that starved are not counted. A world far to the right and low loses much, but in small pieces; a world high up loses whole branches. The dashed line is the criterion's line.
culls.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From every phase of every living world's recorded frames, read by `research/screen/culls.py` into `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/screen/culls/<run>.json`, and scored by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.

1. Rebuild the network as each phase left it, just before its cleanup: the frame before, changed as the phase's record says (newborns and their links, links handed over, searches, lapsed links).
2. Of the agents the cleanup removed, tell those that starved from those culled: an agent linked to a survivor, or that held nothing (in a game nothing staked on it; in reproduction what it had, less its child, its gifts, its mates' dues and its upkeep), starved; the run's counts of the starved and the culled settle the agents the record leaves open, and any still open count as culled.
3. Group the culled by their links (under mend_on_death, by the piece of the network they were cut off in): the pieces culled; the largest counts.
4. Across: the share of the network culled in all, averaged over the phases. Up: how many phases culled a piece of more than 15%, every 100 iterations.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py healthorder`.

halves.title: Healthier or sicker with time?
halves.caption: Each dot is a living world: its health scored over the first half of its run (iterations 100 to the middle) and over the second (the middle to the end). Above the dashed diagonal a world grew healthier; below it, sicker.
halves.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From the screen's readings of every world, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/screen/worlds/<run>.json` (research/screen/measures.py: every iteration's statistics, every 25th iteration's frame, every kept world), scored by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.
